full_judgment:
Mr. A.B.M. Khairul Haque, J.: This appeal arises out of a judgment and order dated 21.12.1986 and decree dates 8.1.1987, passed by the Subordinate Judge, Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka, in dismissing the Money Suit No. 78 of 1985. 

 3. At the hearing of the suit, the learned Judge framed the following issues: a) Is the suit maintainable in its pre-sent form? b) Is the plaintiff entitled to get a decree as prayed for? c) To what relief, if any, is the plain-tiff entitled? 3(A). The plaintiff bank in support of his claim examined one of its officers. Md. Golam Rahman Senior Officer. He as P.W. 1 stated the plaint case that on the prayer of the defendant the plaintiff bank opened three Letters of Credit to import fabrics and on receipt of the shipping documents they asked the defendant to retire those but the defendant failed to do so, rather, requested the bank to arrange for release of the merchandise from the port and store in the godown on creation of a loan being loan against imported merchandise (LIM), accordingly the plaintiff bank on payment of the requisite taxes released the goods through its approved C and F agent and brought the goods at Dhaka. But the defendant failed to take delivery of the said merchandise in spite of repeated notices and remainders, as such, by publication of notice in the newspapers they sold the same and adjusted the sale proceeds against the dues of the bank. He denies that the price of the merchandise was Tk. 15.00,000/-. In his cross-examination he admitted that he did not see the merchandise but deposed on the basis of records kept in his office. He further stated that on the instruction of the defendant, the plaintiff bank, through its clearing agent, released the goods but he denied that the defendant paid Tk. 20,000/-. He further stated that he contacted the defendant in his address at 88, Laboratory Road on 25.1.1983. He admit-ted that in the letter dated 29.12.1982 of the defendant the address of 88, Laboratory Road was mentioned. He further stated that he could not inform the defendant about the public auction of the merchandise in his said address because at that time they were not aware of the same but they informed him in his earlier address. He further stated that the tender to sell the merchandise was first published on 7.4.1978 and the said tender was opened on 18.4.1978 but subsequently the merchandise was sold on 9.7.1981. He denied that at the time of sale the market value of the aforesaid merchandise was Tk. 7.50,000/- He also reiterated that after sale, the price of the imported merchandise was adjusted against the dues of the bank. P.W. 2 Md. Humayun Kabir Majumdar is also an officer of the plaintiff Bank. He stated in his examination-in-chief that the defendant imported the fabrics by opening letters of credit but when he failed to take delivery of the said goods they took steps to sell those merchandise through advertisement in the newspapers both Bengali and English but since no tender was submit-ted in response to public notice, they were constrained to sell those merchandise on negotiation at Tk. 75,001/-. After the sell, the defendant by his letter dated 29.12.1982 wanted to know the position of his account and accordingly he was informed and was asked to repay the dues of the Bank but when he failed to repay, the bank was constrained to institute the suit for recovery of its outstanding dues. The witness stated that he was an officer in the local office of the bank, that they asked the defendant to take delivery of the goods verbally but could not elaborate as to which officer said so. He further stated that 300% tax was realized from them on 1.8.1977 and 200% tax 6.10.1977 and that they paid the tax properly on behalf of the defendant. 

 7. Mr. Shaheed Alam, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant firstly submits that it was the duty of the defendant to retire the ship-ping documents from the plaintiff bank on payment of the dues of the bank but on the request of the defendant, the bank had to arrange release of the goods on payment of the requisite duties and taxes to the Customs Authorities and stored the imported merchandise in the godown at Dhaka. But in spite of repeated remainders the defendants failed to take delivery of the goods on payment of the dues of the bank. As such, the bank had no other alternative but to sale the imported merchandise and adjust the sale-proceeds against the dues of the bank and although tender was invited but ultimately sold on negotiation at Tk. 75,001/- and since there was no response from the defendant. the plaintiff bank was constrained to sell the imported goods. He further submits that the bank not only settled the overseas dues but also paid all the duties and taxes on his behalf but in no time the defendant came forward to settle his accounts with the bank. As such after selling the said merchandise in the available highest price, the bank was constrained to institute the suit for recovery of the rest of its dues and is entitled to get the decree as prayed for.
